religion_note: ABS 2021 religious affiliation; the question is voluntary and 'not stated' is retained as its own category.
ancestry_note: ABS ancestry is multi-response (up to two per person); these shares are of all the responses given, not of people, so they sum to 100%.
language_note: ABS 2021 language used at home (G13), one answer per person, at the outermost level of the ABS classification; 'not stated' is retained as its own category.
sex_ratio_note: Males per 100 females among the 25,026 people counted in the 2021 Census at their usual address here (12,770 males, 12,259 females; ABS G01). The ABS adjusts each count at random by a few people to protect confidentiality, so the males and females make 25,029 rather than 25,026.
median_age_note: The ABS's own median age of persons for this area (2021 Census, G02), published in whole years; the census counts people at their usual address.
ethnicity_note: Ancestry, which is what Australia's census asks in place of an ethnicity question ('What is the person's ancestry?'), coded by the ABS to its Standard Classification of Cultural and Ethnic Groups. Up to two ancestries are recorded for each person, and each share is the percentage of the 25,026 people here who reported that ancestry: the 32,910 responses exceed the people, so the shares sum to more than 100, as in the ABS's own QuickStats. G08 names 30 ancestries; every other one is in 'Other', and 'Not stated' is people who gave none. ABS 2021 Census, G08 (total responses).

adapter_hint: ABS 2021 Census (religion, ancestry): python -m scripts.fetch_census.abs --level lga
religion_note: ABS 2021 religious affiliation; the question is voluntary and 'not stated' is retained as its own category.
ancestry_note: ABS ancestry is multi-response (up to two per person); these shares are of all the responses given, not of people, so they sum to 100%.
language_note: ABS 2021 language used at home (G13), one answer per person, at the outermost level of the ABS classification; 'not stated' is retained as its own category.
sex_ratio_note: Males per 100 females among the 14,229 people counted in the 2021 Census at their usual address here (7,112 males, 7,119 females; ABS G01). The ABS adjusts each count at random by a few people to protect confidentiality, so the males and females make 14,231 rather than 14,229.
median_age_note: The ABS's own median age of persons for this area (2021 Census, G02), published in whole years; the census counts people at their usual address.
ethnicity_note: Ancestry, which is what Australia's census asks in place of an ethnicity question ('What is the person's ancestry?'), coded by the ABS to its Standard Classification of Cultural and Ethnic Groups. Up to two ancestries are recorded for each person, and each share is the percentage of the 14,229 people here who reported that ancestry: the 19,829 responses exceed the people, so the shares sum to more than 100, as in the ABS's own QuickStats. G08 names 30 ancestries; every other one is in 'Other', and 'Not stated' is people who gave none. ABS 2021 Census, G08 (total responses).

adapter_hint: ABS 2021 Census (religion, ancestry): python -m scripts.fetch_census.abs --level lga
religion_note: ABS 2021 religious affiliation; the question is voluntary and 'not stated' is retained as its own category.
ancestry_note: ABS ancestry is multi-response (up to two per person); these shares are of all the responses given, not of people, so they sum to 100%.
language_note: ABS 2021 language used at home (G13), one answer per person, at the outermost level of the ABS classification; 'not stated' is retained as its own category.
sex_ratio_note: Males per 100 females among the 292,011 people counted in the 2021 Census at their usual address here (147,444 males, 144,566 females; ABS G01). The ABS adjusts each count at random by a few people to protect confidentiality, so the males and females make 292,010 rather than 292,011.
median_age_note: The ABS's own median age of persons for this area (2021 Census, G02), published in whole years; the census counts people at their usual address.
ethnicity_note: Ancestry, which is what Australia's census asks in place of an ethnicity question ('What is the person's ancestry?'), coded by the ABS to its Standard Classification of Cultural and Ethnic Groups. Up to two ancestries are recorded for each person, and each share is the percentage of the 292,011 people here who reported that ancestry: the 364,915 responses exceed the people, so the shares sum to more than 100, as in the ABS's own QuickStats. G08 names 30 ancestries; every other one is in 'Other', and 'Not stated' is people who gave none. ABS 2021 Census, G08 (total responses).
